title: "Benchmarks against other software"
description: "RI-constrained reciprocal spectral matching, peak areas and acid-profile recovery in a reproducible 16-sample GC–MS comparison."

## Sixteen simulated chromatograms

Each sample contains 1,200 scans and 258 mass channels. The 48 reference
spectra retain the RI metadata supplied with <code>L0glm::simulatedSpectra</code>.
A monotone retention-time–RI map places the compounds along the chromatogram.
Their presence varies across samples, giving 380 true occurrences.

One compound has a broad, acid-like profile. The remaining compounds have
exponentially modified Gaussian profiles. Increasing concentration broadens
both types towards later times while keeping the leading edge approximately
fixed. A small positive drift shifts successive samples to the right.
The signal also contains a smooth background and quasi-Poisson noise with
dispersion 2.

GCMSprime estimates its PSF from the chromatograms and uses the generating
dispersion for this comparison. The simulation’s calibration maps are used
to score the recovered spectra.

| Method | Seconds | TP | FP | F1 |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GCMSprime | 70.48 | 372 | 2 | 0.987 |
| MS-DIAL | 21.08 | 364 | 56 | 0.910 |
| mzmine | 41.83 | 348 | 91 | 0.850 |
| eRah | 10.73 | 347 | 258 | 0.705 |
| AMDIS | 36.04 | 351 | 492 | 0.574 |
| xcms + CAMERA | 26.97 | 349 | 34 | 0.915 |
| MSHub | 14.56 | 331 | 422 | 0.584 |

Times are wall-clock analysis times on an HP ZBook Fury G8 with an Intel
Core i9-11950H, eight physical cores and 16 logical threads. AMDIS runs
serially and xcms + CAMERA uses four sample workers. Input conversion time
is recorded separately in the downloadable tables.

## Reciprocal spectral matches and integrated areas

Each recovered spectrum is compared with all 48 reference spectra,
including compounds absent from that sample. Candidates must lie within
30 RI units and have cosine similarity of at least 0.70. A pair is retained
when the recovered and reference spectra select each other as their best
eligible hit. Equal cosine scores are ordered by RI difference and then ID.

A true positive is a reciprocal hit to a compound present in the sample.
All other called components count as false positives, and each missed
true occurrence counts as a false negative. The RI calibration follows
the known generating map, including sample drift. MSHub's aligned outputs
use the corresponding mean reference clock.

[![Estimated versus true peak areas for reciprocal RI-constrained hits](../reference/figures/simulated-16-area-predictions.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-area-predictions.png)

The area plots use the recorded area of each selected true match. Both axes
are on the log10 scale. Each panel shows adjusted R², the number of contributing
matches and a 95% prediction interval. Areas retain their engine's native units.
The dashed 1:1 line applies to integrated counts.

Model-ion areas also depend on the relative abundance of the chosen ion.
Their global R² therefore combines integration accuracy with differences
in spectral response across compounds. The full results also report area
errors across samples after removing each compound's native response factor.

[![Reciprocal spectral cosine hits with individual points on a logit axis](../reference/figures/simulated-16-spectral-violin.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-spectral-violin.png)

The violin plot includes all reciprocal hits within the RI window. Crosses
identify hits to compounds absent from that sample. The tick labels retain
the original cosine units on the logit-spaced axis.

### Additional AMDIS calls

AMDIS returned **843 components**, of which **351** were reciprocal
hits to true occurrences. **489 additional calls** shared their best eligible
reference hit with another call in the same sample. Its area regression
has adjusted R² **0.840**, conditional on the 351 selected true matches;
these are the individual returned areas, without adding duplicate calls.

Area agreement is calculated for selected true matches. Every additional
call contributes to the false-positive count, including extra spectra whose
best eligible library hit is the same compound. The saved identification
table records these alternatives, so the area and spectral scores can be
read alongside the number of components called.

## One simulated chromatogram

[![Observed and true mean signals for a simulated sample](../reference/figures/simulated-16-sample-heatmap.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-sample-heatmap.png)

This is the first sample containing the acid-like compound. The two panels

## Acid-like peak profiles across samples

[![True and recovered acid-like profiles across samples](../reference/figures/simulated-16-acid-profiles.png)](../reference/figures/simulated-16-acid-profiles.png)

Colours identify samples. Dashed curves show the true profiles, and solid
curves show compatible returned components, each scaled to its own maximum.
Thin curves are additional calls to the same reference compound.
Retention indices place the profiles on a common axis while preserving
concentration-dependent broadening. The panels use each engine's exported
profile type. mzmine and MSHub export spectra and areas without per-component
scan profiles in this workflow.

## Reproduce the comparison

[GCMSbenchmark](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime/tree/master/GCMSbenchmark)
includes the seeded simulation, full reference library, engine settings,
scoring tables and code to recreate the figures. Its
[installation guide](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime/blob/master/GCMSbenchmark/INSTALL.md)
covers the R packages, external engines and platform requirements.

Download the [summary table](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime/blob/master/GCMSbenchmark/inst/benchmarks/results/benchmark.csv),
[matched pairs](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime/blob/master/GCMSbenchmark/inst/benchmarks/results/matches.csv)
or [all component identifications](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime/blob/master/GCMSbenchmark/inst/benchmarks/results/identifications.csv).

## Comparison with other software

GCMSprime combines a formally **estimated time-varying point-spread function
(PSF)** with **compound-specific peak shapes**, **grouped peak selection
across mass channels** and a **mathematically specified information
criterion** for automatic compound-count selection.

For its default quasi-Poisson model, the fitted mean and variance satisfy
\(\operatorname{Var}(Y_{it})=\phi\mu_{it}\). The final quasi-GIC combines
the corresponding fit criterion with a penalty for the number of compounds
and their occurrences. Grouped L0 selection uses the mass channels jointly,
and hard log-concavity constrains each component profile. This combination
distinguishes GCMSprime from every evaluated configuration. The other
workflows use peak detection, representative ion traces, correlations,
local covariance, factorization of peak integrals or PARAFAC2 least squares.
Their preprocessing noise estimates and selection rules are summarized below.
[Mathematical basis](algorithm.html)

| Workflow | How it deconvolves and where that can limit recovery | Access |
|:--------|:----------------------------------|:-------------|
| GCMSprime | Estimates a time-varying PSF and uses grouped L0 selection across ions to call peaks. A log-concave factor model fits compound-specific profiles, full spectra and smooth background, with GIC or quasi-GIC selecting the compound count. Samples can share spectra while retaining their own profiles. | Free, GPL open source. [Repository](https://github.com/tomwenseleers/GCMSprime) |
| MS-DIAL | Extracts spectra from detected model peaks within each run, then aligns the features. Smoothing, detection thresholds and the deconvolution window affect which components are recovered. [GC–MS tutorial](https://github.com/systemsomicslab/mtbinfo.github.io/blob/master/MS-DIAL/tutorial.md) | Free, LGPL-3 source. Some vendor readers have separate terms. [MsdialWorkbench](https://github.com/systemsomicslab/MsdialWorkbench#source-code-license) |
| mzmine / ADAP-GC | The benchmark’s GC-EI module groups resolved ions by retention time and shape similarity. Pseudospectra depend on upstream detection, the grouping thresholds and the minimum number of ions. Batch alignment follows extraction. [GC-EI guide](https://mzmine.github.io/mzmine_documentation/latest/module_docs/featdet_spectraldeconvolutiongc/spectraldeconvolutiongc.html) | Free Community licence for eligible academic users. Commercial use requires a paid plan. [Public source](https://github.com/mzmine/mzmine#license) · [Plans](https://mzio.io/plans/) |
| xcms + CAMERA | Detects ion peaks first and then groups them into pseudospectra. Filter widths and grouping rules affect the coverage of weak and coeluting peaks. CAMERA was developed for LC–MS feature annotation. [Kuhl et al. (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1021/ac202450g) | Free, GPL open source. [xcms](https://bioconductor.org/packages/xcms) · [CAMERA](https://bioconductor.org/packages/CAMERA) |
| eRah | Uses local covariance and orthogonal signal deconvolution after filtering and baseline removal. Recovery depends on width and signal thresholds. Cross-sample alignment follows per-sample deconvolution. [eRah manual](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/erah/vignettes/erah-manual.html) | Free, GPL open source. [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=erah) |
| AMDIS | Uses representative ion traces as model peak shapes within each chromatogram. Component width, sensitivity and shape settings govern the calls and extracted spectra. [NIST guide](https://chemdata.nist.gov/mass-spc/amdis/docs/amdis.pdf) | Free standalone binary. [NIST distribution](https://chemdata.nist.gov/dokuwiki/doku.php?id=chemdata%3Aamdis) |
| GNPS/MSHub | Requires a sample series for its NMF workflow. It factorizes aligned peak integrals, so the model resolves spectra and abundances from variation across samples and drops the scan-level profile information. [Aksenov et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0700-3) · [Workflow guide](https://ccms-ucsd.github.io/GNPSDocumentation/gc-ms-deconvolution/) | Free hosted workflow with a GNPS account. Public source under the repository’s nonprofit-use licence. [Source](https://github.com/CCMS-UCSD/GNPS_Workflows/tree/master/mshub-gc) · [Licence](https://github.com/CCMS-UCSD/GNPS_Workflows/blob/733ed89372c3754a4c4d132319da5b4313c47288/LICENSE) |
| PARADISe | Fits PARAFAC2 within retention intervals. Intervals and ranks can require review, and the constant cross-product constraint restricts how peak overlap can change across samples. [Johnsen et al. (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chroma.2017.04.052) · [Protocol](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-2143/v1) | Free Community and paid Professional editions. [Kromath](https://www.kromath.com/) |
